source.title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs

accepted.question_text: Let G(2n,r) be the class of simple r-regular graphs on 2n vertices, let phi(k,G) be the number of k-matchings in G, let K_{r,r} be the complete bipartite r-regular graph on 2r vertices, and let qK_{r,r} be the disjoint union of q copies of K_{r,r}. Is it true, for every r, q, and k = 1,...,qr, that qK_{r,r} maximizes the number of k-matchings among all simple r-regular graphs on 2qr vertices, equivalently Theta(k,qr,r) = phi(k,qK_{r,r})?

evidence.quote: The upper matching conjecture, abbreviated as UMC, states [23] Θ(k, qr, r) = φ(k, qKr,r) for k = 1, . . . , qr.

accepted.question_text: Let G_{bi,mult}(2n,r) be the class of bipartite r-regular multigraphs on 2n vertices and let lambda(k,n,r) be the minimum, over that class, of the number of k-matchings. Is the lower matching conjecture true, namely that for every k = 1,...,n, lambda(k,n,r) is at least binom(n,k)^2 times ((nr-k)/nr)^(rn-k) times (kr/n)^k?

evidence.quote: The lower matching conjecture, abbreviated here as LMC, states [23] λ(k, n, r) ≥ (n choose k)^2((nr − k)/nr)^(rn−k)(kr/n)^k for k = 1, . . . , n.

accepted.question_text: Let omega(n,n,r) be the minimum number of perfect matchings among r-colorable r-regular multigraphs on 2n vertices, in the notation of the source. For each fixed r >= 3, does omega(n,n,r) grow exponentially as n tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Perfect matchings in non-bipartite regular multigraphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.1. ω(n, n, r) has an exponential growth in n for a fixed r ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: For an infinite r-regular graph G, let h_G(p) be its p-matching entropy, where p is the limiting density of vertices covered by matchings. Is h_G(p) always at most the p-matching entropy of a countable disjoint union of copies of K_{r,r}, for every p in [0,1]?

evidence.quote: The asymptotic matching conjecture, abbreviated as AUMC, states that G satisfies hG(p) ≤ h∞Kr,r (p) for all p ∈ [0, 1].

accepted.question_text: For an infinite bipartite r-regular graph G, let h_G(p) be its p-matching entropy. Is h_G(p) always at least f(p,r) = 1/2 times (p log r - p log p - 2(1-p) log(1-p) + (r-p) log(1-p/r)) for every p in [0,1]? The source explicitly reports this asymptotic lower matching conjecture as proved in the cited literature.

evidence.quote: The asymptotic lower matching conjecture, abbreviated ALMC, claims that for any r-regular bipartite infinite graph G the following inequality holds [23]: hG(p) ≥ f(p, r) for all p ∈ [0, 1].
The proof of the ALMC is given in [27].

accepted.question_text: In the non-bipartite regular multigraph setting of the source, let omega(k,n,r) denote the minimum number of k-matchings in the relevant r-regular multigraph class. For fixed r >= 2 and fixed density p in (0,2/3), does omega(k,n,r) grow exponentially in n for every integer k in the interval [pn, 2n/3], and what are sharp or useful lower bounds for that exponential growth rate?

evidence.quote: It is natural to conjecture that for any p ∈ (0, 2/3) and an integer k ∈ [pn, 2n/3] ω(k, n, r) has an exponential growth in n for a fixed r ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: Let Psi_{2n} be Edmonds's perfect-matching polytope inside the symmetric doubly stochastic 2n by 2n zero-diagonal matrices, and let haf_k(B) be the k-haffnian of B. For k = 2,...,n, determine mu_{k,n} = min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), or at least give good lower bounds for this minimum.

evidence.quote: Our problem is to find or give a good lower bound for min B∈Ψ2n hafk(B) = µk,n for k = 2, . . . , n.

accepted.question_text: With mu_{k,n} = min_{B in Psi_{2n}} haf_k(B), is the uniform complete-graph matrix (1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n}) always a minimizer, so that mu_{k,n} = haf_k((1/(2n-1))A(K_{2n})) for every k = 2,...,n? The source explicitly resolves this proposed exact formula negatively for k = n and sufficiently large n.

evidence.quote: However for k = n and n big enough (6.3) is wrong as explained below.

accepted.question_text: Let mu = lim_{n to infinity} log(mu_{n,n})/n, where mu_{n,n} is the minimum of haf_n(B) over B in Psi_{2n}. Is mu greater than negative infinity, equivalently does mu_{n,n} have at least an exponential-in-n lower bound rather than superexponential decay?
accepted.context_brief: Weak van der Waerden analog for haffnians

evidence.quote: A weak analog of the van der Waerden conjecture is the claim that µ > −∞.

accepted.question_text: For arbitrary infinite r-regular graphs that need not be bipartite, what is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for p-matching entropy at densities p in [0,2/3]? In particular, what explicit lower-bound function should h_G(p) satisfy in that non-bipartite setting?

evidence.quote: There should be a similar inequality for infinite r-regular graphs, at least for p ∈ [0, 2/3] as we explain in §7. However we do not have the precise version of such inequality.

accepted.question_text: For infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges, what is the correct analog of the asymptotic lower matching conjecture for matching entropy?

evidence.quote: Second, what is the analog of the ALMC for infinite cubic connected graphs with no bridges?

trace.notes: Normalized the input as one zbMATH URL. The zbMATH web page was Cloudflare-challenged in local curl, so the record was resolved through zbMATH API metadata to the exact work with arXiv 1112.5632, DOI 10.13001/1081-3810.1577, and EMIS link 34020. The readable primary source used for extraction was the EMIS PDF.

Mapped the PDF into sections: introduction with notation and main conjectures; preliminary haffnian/permanent definitions; upper bounds; van der Waerden/Tverberg lower-bound material; positive hyperbolic polynomial method; non-bipartite graph problems; and infinite regular graph entropy problems.
Extracted UMC, LMC, Conjecture 1.1, AUMC, ALMC, and the remark that a corresponding non-bipartite entropy inequality is not precisely known.

Extracted the non-bipartite partial-matching exponential-growth conjecture, the haffnian minimum problem, the proposed but refuted complete-graph minimizer formula, and the weak haffnian van der Waerden analog.
